changelog:
A subtitle track named simply **Signs** is now recognised as a signs track. If the plugin was
switching your subtitles off on a dubbed anime, this is why.

## 🐛 Fixed

- **A signs track called "Signs" was missed.** 1.3.1.0 read the track title to spot an anime
  signs track, but it only looked for the *pair*: `Signs & Songs`, `Songs and Signs`, or the
  `S&S` / `S+S` / `SnS` abbreviations. A great many releases ship the track named just
  **Signs**, **Signs Only** or **English Signs** — those all fell through.

  The effect was the opposite of subtle. With English audio, English in your subtitle list and
  an `English Signs` track, the plugin saw two ordinary complete English subtitle tracks,
  decided the English audio already covered you, looked for a forced track to fall back on,
  found none, and **switched subtitles off** — losing exactly the on-screen text that track
  exists to provide.

  If you worked around it by turning *Prefer non-forced subtitles* off, you can turn it back
  on. With both subtitle options at their defaults you now get the signs track on a dubbed
  anime and no subtitles at all on a film in a language you read.

- Complete tracks are still complete: `Dialogue + Signs` and `Full Subtitles + Signs` are not
  read as signs tracks, and `Designs` is still not mistaken for one.

- **The configuration page said otherwise.** Both subtitle hints promised that "Signs & Songs
  (S&S)" tracks were covered, which is what set an expectation the code did not meet. They now
  name the shapes actually recognised.

## ⬆️ Upgrading

Straight upgrade from 1.3.1.0 — no configuration changes. Server compatibility is unchanged
(**Jellyfin 12.x**); 10.11 servers stay on 1.2.0.1.

Still not detected: a signs track whose title is translated (e.g. *Panneaux*), and a track
named only **Songs**. The latter is deliberate — on a concert recording a "Songs" track is the
whole content, not a signs-style extra. If your releases use names that are missed, open an
issue with the exact track titles.

## 🔧 Under the hood

- One regex alternation, next to the existing forced-keyword check in `LanguageHelper`, so
  every place that already understood forced subtitles picks this up with no other change.
- The two track titles from the field report are now test cases, in both their raw and
  Jellyfin-composed (`- Default - ASS`) forms, alongside an end-to-end test of the dub
  scenario they came from.
